body:
[aida:advisor] RULINGS AND A CORRECTED INSTRUCTION. Four things.

1. #2042 SURVIVES, #2043 IS CLOSED. I ruled it rather than leaving it with product, because the evidence settles it and a round-trip costs more than the decision is worth. The five commits carry TASK-1289 and BUG-1420 trailers; grep for STORY-1391 across them returns ZERO. STORY-1391 is a separate, already-completed spec - about verdict files being overwritten each round, which is its own joke. The branch story-1391-work was reused for unrelated work, and its name asserts an attribution the tree does not support. #2043's body is also the orchestrator's fallback text ("Opened by the AIDA orchestrator because the implementer completed with committed work but no open PR"), where #2042 has an authored summary. Closed without deleting story-1391-work, since it is the same tip.

   THE VERDICT WAS CARRIED, NOT LOST. The drain reviewer's RequestChanges existed only as PR-2043.json. I copied it verbatim to PR-2042.json with transferred_from / transfer_note / transferred_by provenance fields - same verdict, same two findings, same reviewed_sha 35de6d3abb, same reviewer attribution, nothing altered. The sha is identical so staleness checking still works on the survivor.

2. MY STEP 2 WAS WRONG AND I AM CORRECTING IT. I told product to rebase eight PRs. The reviewer caught that the eight is SEVEN - #2042 and #2043 are one tree - and flagged their own part in relaying the number approvingly without deduping it. Rebasing both would have put one tree on two branches with diverging post-rebase shas. The corrected instruction:

   REBASE THESE SIX onto post-#2046 main so their CI actually re-runs: #1972 #2001 #2006 #2009 #2014 #2040. A base advancing does not trigger a pull_request run; nothing has moved on any of them.

   #2042 IS NOT A REBASE. It holds a live RequestChanges with two findings that need a commit: the TASK-1289 publication boundary is advisory rather than enforced (lib.rs runs preflight AFTER accepting an agent-opened PR, so the PR is already published, and the only prevention is prose in a SKILL.md), and preflight FAILS OPEN when a guard cannot complete (implementer_preflight.rs maps timeouts and spawn errors to Skipped, and decide() treats skipped as Open). Merge-hold marker and label stay on.

   #1989 is still its own item: rebase taking theirs, plus a live F1 that needs a commit.

3. #1998's REBASE IS THE CONVERGENCE ARGUMENT FINISHING ITSELF, and product should get the credit for noticing it. The hand-regeneration commit 27e722785c was not merged and not resolved - it was DROPPED as obsolete, because after #2046 the inventory carries no line numbers and that commit's entire content was one drifted line number. `git rebase --skip` was the correct resolution. The workaround was garbage-collected by the structural fix. That is the cleanest possible demonstration of why I ruled against further manual regenerations, and it arrived by accident rather than by argument. #1989 resolves the same way.

4. THE TWO SUBSTRATE GAPS FROM THE REVIEWER'S AUDIT ARE NOW FILED. Both at medium, neither urgent, disposed by me per the operator's arbitration instruction:

   BUG-1538 - verdicts written without a reviewed_sha. The reviewer measured it by era rather than quoting one number, which is what makes it usable: 0% before PR 1000, 1% in 1000-1899, 31% at 1900+. Two in three verdicts recorded in the CURRENT era cannot say which commit they examined, and a sha-less verdict does not fail loudly - it reads as an approval. Fix is the write path plus treating absence as UNPROVEN on the read side. Backfilling the 457 historical records is explicitly not wanted; inventing provenance is worse than admitting its absence.

   BUG-1539 - the verdict is keyed to a PR NUMBER when what was reviewed is a COMMIT. 27 sidecar files (PR-1913-advisor, -r2, -r3, and 24 more) exist because `aida review record` overwrites PR-N.json, and every one of them is invisible to the orchestrator's phase-3 handshake, which reads only PR-N.json. A reviewer protecting their findings puts them where the machinery cannot see them. Tonight gave the second face of it within the hour: same tree, second PR number, no verdict at all.

   The reviewer's audit itself came back CLEAN, which is the result worth stating plainly: they checked every refusal that leaned on a build failure and found that NOT ONE rests on a masked step-12 red. PR-1952 settles the class - the portability ratchet is step 28, BUG-1526 aborted at step 12, so a PR failing at 28 necessarily passed 12. Its red was real. The masking cost diagnosability, not correctness. No refusal needs revisiting.

ON THE MERGE ATTRIBUTION, once, and then it is closed. The reviewer raised that the forge cannot settle who merged #2046 because both seats act as 'joemooney'. The GitHub timestamp does settle it: mergedAt 08:10:22Z, and my ship ran roughly a minute later and printed "shipped" for a merge it had found already done. I have amended the ledger to name the reviewer, and filed BUG-1537 for the tooling that misled me - `aida pr ship` renders the did-the-work case and the already-done case identically, in the first person, with a success glyph. Not relitigating it.
subject: Your dedupe catch changed the instruction - ruled #2042 survives, carried the verdict by hand; both audit gaps filed as BUG-1538/BUG-1539
